newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian investment tax to be around 12.5pct - Visco.
newsitem.headline: Italian investment tax to be around 12.5pct - Visco.

text.p: The Italian government intends to introduce a tax on investments of around 12.5 percent to quarantee fiscal uniformity for financial instruments, Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco said in a magazine interview.
Visco told parliament in June he wanted to introduce later this year a more systematic approach to the taxation of gains on all financial products.
"The aim is that of fiscal neutrality," Visco said in an interview with Panorama magazine released ahead of publication on Thursday.

"The rate (for the investment tax) will therefore be near to 12.5 percent, which is the same level as that imposed on government bonds. Initially however there will be two or three different rates," he added.
Interest on government bonds are currently subject to a 12.5 percent withholding tax, although foreign investors in new bond issues are exempt from this tax.
Investors in equities can currently opt to pay a two percent 'forfeit' tax on capital gains, which do not have to be declared in detail and are therefore hard to check. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
